fact: ITWeb Africa, citing LINX, reports that LINX Nairobi, an IXP reachable from multiple Nairobi data centres and launched in 2023, now supports more than 55 active networks.
ITWeb Africa, citing LINX, lists TikTok among the platforms active on the LINX Nairobi exchange (alongside Starlink).
Traffic: more than 330 Gbps (peak) at LINX Nairobi and LINX Mombasa combined on 2026-07-10 (the article gives no peak date; the figure is the peak reached over the past year), per the companies.
The companies say combined traffic across the two Kenyan LINX exchange points rose twentyfold over the past year, reaching a peak above 330 Gbps (no starting figure given).

LINX operates two interconnected exchange points in Kenya, Nairobi and Mombasa; a cloud provider connected to Mombasa in 2025 and to Nairobi in 2026, and both are described as providing routing options.
Packet Clearing House lists KIXP in Nairobi as an active association-run exchange point managed by TESPOK, established February 2001; no members or traffic figures are given.
iColo and TESPOK state that KIXP, run by TESPOK, is the largest and most established IXP in East Africa, exchanging traffic among networks, ISPs and content providers.

iColo announced on this date that KIXP has entered its Mombasa MBA2 data centre with a new point of presence, giving KIXP presence in Mombasa as well as its existing sites; over 100 networks are connected at iColo's Mombasa campus.
iColo states LINX launched its first African IXP, LINX Nairobi, a year before this announcement (launch month not given).

Developing Telecoms reports that the iXAfrica NBOX1 data centre in Nairobi connects to multiple internet exchanges including LINX Nairobi and KIXP, and that KIXP announced a peering point (PoP) there, to localise exchange traffic.
LINX announced that LINX Mombasa, a multi-site IXP in the iColo MBA1 and MBA2 data centres in Mombasa, is ready for business, after LINX Nairobi launched just over 12 months earlier.
LINX states LINX Mombasa in Mombasa is a second exchange point in service in Kenya alongside LINX Nairobi in Nairobi, the first IXP with a physical presence in both cities.

DCNN reports LINX Nairobi, launched November 2023, is operating with local ISPs (ICON Fiber, Mtaani Telecom, Mymanga Networks, PepeaNet), global content networks and partners interconnected and traffic starting to build; no figure given.
DCNN reports global content networks such as Meta are present at LINX Nairobi, peering with local ISPs.

Africa Data Centres' NB01 data sheet says it offers free peering with KIXP (Kenya Internet eXchange Point) at its Nairobi facility; the document gives no member count and dates itself only by its published date 2021-02-11.

Liquid Intelligent Technologies' release says the Kenya Internet Exchange Point (KIXP) is housed at the East Africa Data Centre; no member count or traffic given; date is the release's published date 2017-05-16.
TechnoMag says Starlink's Nairobi gateway at the icolo.io facility peers at KIXP; no member count or traffic given.
